samples.source: And so I'm going to take us back to 1706 and we have a guy named John Machin. This guy was a real seriously crazy guy. He used the formula on the top and the standard arctangent series there and he computed by hand on paper 100 digits of pi.

samples.source: How many people have heard of the dining philosophers problem? Okay, we got quite a few. And, you know, you've got these philosophers, represented by brown circles, because I'm not that great at graphics. And now, Dijkstra, when he posed this in 1969, said that there was some very difficult spaghetti, so he had to have two forks to eat it. And I haven't come across any spaghetti like that during my entire life. So I'm moving it eastwards a little bit, and we're using chopsticks instead. And for chopsticks I have had the experience of requiring two of them to eat unless I can stab it or something.
samples.before_display: 有多少人听说过“哲学家就餐问题”？好，不少人。这些棕色圆圈代表哲学家。没办法，我画图就这个水平。Dijkstra 在 1969 年提出这个问题时，说有一种特别难对付的意大利面，得用两把叉子才能吃。活到现在，我还真没遇到过这种面。所以，我把背景稍微往东挪一点，改用筷子。筷子我倒有经验，得用两根才能吃。当然，拿一根直接戳，又是另一回事。
